I like systems I can take apart, understand and rebuild. At home I run my own three-node Proxmox lab and test everything there first.

ai_pairs.q: How do I free up a full PBS datastore?
ai_pairs.a: Run a prune job to apply your retention, then garbage collection to actually free the chunks.

ai_pairs.q: Share or NTFS permissions — which one wins?
ai_pairs.a: Both apply and the more restrictive one wins. Leave the share at Full Control and manage access with NTFS.

ai_pairs.q: Why won't my VM boot after moving hosts?
ai_pairs.a: Check the CPU type. Set it to x86-64-v2-AES or host so flags like AES are available.

ai_pairs.q: How do I keep IoT devices off my LAN?
ai_pairs.a: Give them their own VLAN, then block IoT → LAN and allow IoT → WAN on the firewall.

ai_pairs.q: Quick way to test a DNS server?
ai_pairs.a: nslookup example.com 10.0.10.53 — if it answers, the server and the port 53 path are fine.

homelab.label: Homelab
homelab.intro: Three Proxmox nodes in my room. Everything runs on my own hardware and is backed up every night.
homelab.flow_desc: Diagram: internet traffic enters through OPNsense and is routed to three Proxmox nodes. Node 1 runs Nginx Proxy Manager, Pi-hole, Vaultwarden, Beszel, Paperless-ngx and PBS. Node 2 runs the LLM VM, LibreChat, Hermes Agent, Ollama and Firecrawl. Node 3 runs n8n, BookStack, wger, WordPress, Anubis and RustDesk.
